es: Redactar normas justas con pasivas modales (must be, may only be, are to be), excepciones (except, apart from), condiciones (on condition that) y una razón breve (in order to, given that).

vocabulary.es: alegando que, por el motivo de que

teaching.en: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, which the committee has marked with a green sign at each entrance.
teaching.es: Los perros deberán llevarse con correa, salvo en la zona vallada, que el comité ha señalado con un cartel verde en cada entrada.
teaching.explanationEs: Except + lugar, tiempo o persona: introduce la excepción. Must be kept: obligación en pasiva.
segments: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area,
which the committee has marked with a green sign at each entrance.
teaching.audioText: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, which the committee has marked with a green sign at each entrance.

teaching.en: Fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily, so the committee considers a blanket ban elsewhere fair.
teaching.es: Las hogueras solo podrán encenderse en la zona señalada, dado que la hierba seca arde con facilidad, por lo que el comité considera justa una prohibición general en el resto.
teaching.explanationEs: Given that + oración: da la razón de la norma. Blanket ban: prohibición que se aplica a todos y a todo, sin matices.
segments: Fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry
grass burns easily, so the committee considers a blanket ban elsewhere fair.
teaching.audioText: Fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily, so the committee considers a blanket ban elsewhere fair.

teaching.en: Bicycles are to be left at the racks in order to keep the paths clear, and the committee may make an exception for deliveries.
teaching.es: Las bicicletas se dejarán en los soportes para mantener despejados los caminos, y el comité podrá hacer una excepción para los repartos.
teaching.explanationEs: In order to + verbo: la finalidad de la norma. Make an exception: permitir algo que normalmente no se permite.
segments: Bicycles are to be left at the racks in order to keep
the paths clear, and the committee may make an exception for deliveries.
teaching.audioText: Bicycles are to be left at the racks in order to keep the paths clear, and the committee may make an exception for deliveries.

teaching.en: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, which is a fair test and easy to apply.
teaching.es: Se podrá poner música siempre que no moleste a otros visitantes, lo que es un criterio justo y fácil de aplicar.
teaching.explanationEs: On condition that + presente: condición formal, más fuerte que if. Fair = justo, equilibrado.
segments: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb
other visitors, which is a fair test and easy to apply.
teaching.audioText: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, which is a fair test and easy to apply.

teaching.en: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the playground, on the grounds that small children could be frightened; it is the only exception.
teaching.es: Salvo los perros guía, ningún animal podrá entrar en el área de juegos, alegando que los niños pequeños podrían asustarse; es la única excepción.
teaching.explanationEs: Apart from + nombre: excepción. On the grounds that + oración: el motivo que se alega para justificar la regla.
segments: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the playground, on the
grounds that small children could be frightened; it is the only exception.
teaching.audioText: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the playground, on the grounds that small children could be frightened; it is the only exception.

teaching.en: A fair rule has a clear reason, a reasonable exception and a responsible person, and the committee will draft it in plain language.
teaching.es: Una norma justa tiene una razón clara, una excepción razonable y un responsable, y el comité la redactará en un lenguaje sencillo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una buena norma tiene razón, excepción razonable y responsable claro. Draft = redactar un borrador.
segments: A fair rule has a clear reason, a reasonable exception and a
responsible person, and the committee will draft it in plain language.

prompt.es: Elige la regla bien redactada con una excepción.

feedback.es: Must be kept es la pasiva correcta y except + lugar introduce la excepción; las otras opciones rompen la pasiva o usan except of.

hint.es: La regla necesita la pasiva: modal + be + participio.

origin.text: The committee wants dogs on a lead in the park, but it accepts one exception: the fenced area, where dogs can run freely.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se permitirán picnics siempre que se lleven la basura a casa.»

feedback.es: On condition that + oración es la fórmula formal de condición.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que sigue a on en la fórmula formal de condición.

origin.text: The committee wants the park to stay clean. Picnics are permitted on ___ that visitors take their rubbish home.

answer.text: Apart from guide dogs, no animals may enter the gardens

feedback.es: Apart from + nombre abre la excepción y después llega la regla general.

hint.es: La excepción abre la frase: Apart from…

prompt.es: Escucha la reunión: ¿a quién se aplica la excepción de las bicicletas?

choices.text: People making deliveries.
Adults with a special card.
Children under ten.

feedback.es: El comité evita la prohibición general de bicicletas haciendo una excepción para los menores de diez años.

origin.audio: At the committee meeting, the chair read out the draft of the new park rules. Dogs must be kept on a lead, she said, except in the fenced area, given that they need space to run. Fires may only be lit in the marked area, and then only with an adult present. Loud music is not banned completely; it may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors. One member objected that a blanket ban on bicycles would be unfair, so the committee agreed to make an exception for children under ten.

prompt.es: Lee el aviso: ¿qué postura refleja el comité?

choices.text: It looks for a compromise rather than a complete ban.
It sides with families with small children against dog owners.
It postpones the decision until residents vote in six months.

feedback.es: Rechaza la prohibición total y propone correa con una zona de excepción: busca un equilibrio entre vecinos con perros y con niños.

origin.text: Notice from the committee: after a long discussion, we decided against a blanket ban on dogs. Instead, dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area. We believe this is a fair balance, given that many residents have dogs and others have small children. The rule will be reviewed after six months.

prompt.es: Escucha el debate y elige qué propone la profesora de música.

choices.text: Banning music at all times.
Allowing music, but only until nine.
Allowing music only at weekends.

feedback.es: Propone permitir la música a condición de que termine a las nueve, en lugar de una prohibición general.

origin.audio: In a community meeting, one neighbour proposed a blanket ban on loud music in the park. Another neighbour, a music teacher, disagreed: she thought the rule should allow music on condition that it stops at nine, given that many families use the park in the evening. The chair suggested combining both ideas, and then asked each speaker to write one sentence that included a reason, so that the committee could compare the proposals fairly.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿por qué pide el presidente una frase con razón a cada uno?

choices.text: To test which neighbour had more supporters.
To persuade the music teacher to drop her idea.
To compare the proposals on equal terms.

feedback.es: Pedir una razón a cada uno permite al comité comparar las propuestas en igualdad de condiciones («so that the committee could compare the proposals fairly»).

origin.text: The summer has been very dry. ___ that the grass burns easily, fires are prohibited.

prompt.es: Escribe tres normas para un parque comunitario con excepciones y una razón.

answer.text: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.
accepted: Rule 1: Dogs must be kept on a lead, except in the fenced area, in order to protect children and other animals, given that some dogs are not used to crowds. Rule 2: Music may be played on condition that it does not disturb other visitors, because the park is a quiet place for many families, and loud music is to be switched off at nine in the evening. Rule 3: Bicycles are to be left at the racks, apart from delivery bikes and children's bikes, so as to keep the main path clear for people on foot. The committee will review all three rules after six months, since a fair rule should change when the park changes. Anyone who disagrees may write to the committee, and please read these rules carefully before you enter.

First, rubbish must be taken home, except on festival days, because the bins are full by noon and the park looks dirty for the next visitors. Second, fires may only be lit in the marked area, given that dry grass burns easily and a single spark could close the whole park for a week. Third, dogs are to be kept on a lead, apart from guide dogs, in order to keep the playground safe for small children, who are often afraid of big animals. Finally, the gates shall be locked at ten unless the committee has approved an event, since neighbours need quiet at night. These rules are fair, because each one has a reason.

feedback.es: Una norma justa une una regla en pasiva, una excepción o condición razonable y una razón que la justifique (in order to, given that, since).

origin.text: Eres miembro del comité de un parque comunitario con un área de juegos, un estanque y un camino principal. Escribe tres normas (entre 130 y 200 palabras en total). Cada una lleva una regla en pasiva (must be, may only be, are to be), una excepción o condición (except, apart from, unless, on condition that) y una razón (in order to, given that, since, so as to).

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿qué quiere decir la presidenta con su última frase?

choices.text: That rules with clear reasons are more likely to be followed.
That rules should work only while people are being watched.
That orders work better than explained rules.

feedback.es: Dice que una norma sin razón es solo una orden y que se obedece únicamente mientras alguien vigila: las normas razonadas se respetan mejor.

origin.audio: After the meeting, the chair summarised why the rules were written the way they were. The aim, she said, was not to ban but to balance: dogs on leads except in the fenced area, music on condition that it ends early, and bicycles allowed apart from on the main path. She added that a rule without a reason is just an order, and people only follow orders while someone is watching.

prompt.es: Lee el correo: ¿qué pide el vecino?

choices.text: A smaller fenced area, to keep the park tidier.
A wider exception to the dog rule at weekends.
The committee's help in measuring the fenced area.

feedback.es: Acepta la norma, pero pide ampliar la excepción de la zona vallada los fines de semana.

origin.text: Dear committee, I agree with the new dog rule in principle, but I think the exception is too narrow. The fenced area is small, and on busy days it is unsafe for big dogs. Could you consider making it bigger, at least at weekends? I would be happy to help measure the space.
